parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no visitor-facing facility or bathroom ban, no documented border/document friction, and no documented police sweeps of visibly trans people. Positives are real: courts struck down local 'propaganda' bans, the Equality Council confirmed a discrimination complaint, and Pride now proceeds under police protection. But the worst documented feature is a tier-1 universal exposure inside custody: a trans man was placed by birth sex in the men's system and held three years in solitary-style isolation with forced strip searches and staff humiliation, the administration denying any violation and no remedy secured (corroborated 2025). Enforcement generally trails statute — hate speech goes unanswered, the bank-denial case produced only a recommendation, and a 2019 arson on an LGBT lawyer went uninvestigated. Social-distance data (79% rejecting LGBT neighbours) is LGBT-wide and resident-facing, so weighted as climate only; no trans-specific violence rate exists, leaving that axis undocumented rather than safe. Sits below the 0.45 anchors on documented hostility, above 0.35 for lacking a truly universal visitor-facing exclusion.
